findings.summary: Feature review 2 of 5 at dcf0346: pass. All five R1 findings are fixed with real-integration evidence, and the marker-v2 change is a genuine runtime fix: the red log at r1-marker-replacement-red.log shows a byte-identical copied marker was accepted before the change. New tests fail closed with quarantine on wrong household key, wrong operator key on an authenticated empty store, marker/log copy, substituted directory, a journal missing an ACKed record, and a durable journal-only intent; each checks disk bytes plus cost and non-cost table hashes. New tests also cover real logout and fresh-login recovery, an obsolete scope after correction and reacceptance (409, stale_scope, history kept), a profile correction (stale_profile, no old capture offers, captured snapshot kept), reconsent with an active second-household control, and a same-CAS capture race across all four outcomes. The root probe now asserts the exact counts failed 1 / cancelled 1 / uncertain 1 / unsupported 0 / captured 4 using hard-coded expectations, not ledger arithmetic. I independently re-checked the runtime against the originals: the cost authority matches generation's lock order (household → consent → founder/session → request → queue projection → profile) and is rechecked after each step. Source validation calls the public generation.read only for eligible terminal jobs, outside the cost transaction and the global serializer. The service checks inventory relationships against migration 013 (one immutable attempt per job; attempt fence = job fence, or job fence − 1 after CancelJob; queued-then-cancelled = fence 1 / version 2) and refuses ACK-without-journal and journal-only records, as the queue-journal delegate and design v1.2 recovery invariants require. Arithmetic and labels agree with 11-A/11-B: unknown is not zero, I1 is stored once, allocation conserves units with an explicit residual, N=0 leaves per-delivered cost undefined, and valued labour stays null. Checks.json and the CUA record bind to dcf0346 and the current cost-journal blob. Coverage read through EOF in this session: the spec (R1), the full diff, current cost-journal and both cost test files (R1 plus the new diff), the root probe, generation-service, queue-journal, founder-auth, migrations 013 and 014, 11-A, 11-B, engineering README and REVIEW_NOTES, and setup-r5. Read only in part: the design (ADR-E03–E06 and the v1.2 invariants), the MODULE_GUIDE WM rows, request-queue (serializeQueueWork and project only), and setup-r1–r4 (verdicts and titles). Not read: review-service, review-journal, review-page, consent-service, child-setup, generation-journal and continuation-journal helpers. The cost slice does not call any of these unread modules; it reads only their tables, the same way generation already does. The protected tests still pass. All real-world gates, full 05-A/B/D/G/11-C and the disclosed limitations remain open.

findings.problem: The brief makes full original reading mandatory before PASS. This session read generation-service, queue-journal, founder-auth, migrations 013/014, 11-A, 11-B and the engineering README/REVIEW_NOTES through EOF. It did not read through EOF: review-service/journal/page, consent-service, child-setup, generation-journal, continuation-journal helpers, the rest of request-queue, the full engineering design (outside ADR-E03–E06 and the v1.2 invariants), MODULE_GUIDE beyond the WM rows, or the setup-r1–r4 bodies. The cost slice calls none of these modules; it reads their tables the same way generation already does. I am disclosing this gap rather than claiming exhaustive coverage. The verdict rests on the cost data path, which I did read in full.

findings.title: Native stale-Saved check at dcf0346 used outage/retry, not held append
findings.problem: At dcf0346 the CUA record shows the Saved message clearing during real journal outage and original-key retries. It does not repeat the held-transport case from the 3b6 finding. The dedicated HTTP-to-DOM held regression ('starting a new in-flight operation clears the previous Saved confirmation') passes in the dcf0346 checks, and d3688b1's native held observation came from a run where cost-page had the same blob. The evidence is adequate, but it is spread across runs.
findings.fix_check: No action needed. Optionally repeat a native held-append observation at the final merge commit.

findings.title: Reconsent test denies through the existing profile-epoch gate
findings.problem: After withdrawal and reconsent (epoch 3), cost denies because child_setup_profiles still carries the old consent_epoch. This is the known same-household reconsent profile limitation, not a cost-specific check on the epoch. The test correctly proves the replay, read and reconcile calls are denied, and that the other household keeps working.
findings.fix_check: Keep the reconsent profile limitation disclosed. No cost change is needed in this slice.
